Codex changelog 2026-08-29: 'Extensions can now inspect or replace MCP tool results before they reach the model'.
Codex changelog 2026-08-27: remote compaction now counts retained images toward its token budget by default, trimming older images as needed.

Claude Code v2.1.238: MCP headersHelper declared in a project .mcp.json, plugin, or agent file now requires folder trust; headersHelper runs without inherited credential env vars; claude plugin install prompts [y/N] before executing a headersHelper.

Anthropic API release notes 2026-08-20: Python SDK v1.0 removes long-deprecated surface including the legacy Text Completions API and the temperature, top_p and top_k parameters on Messages methods; moves httpx to httpx2; async .with_raw_response now needs await response.parse(); AnthropicBedrock raises an error when no AWS region is configured instead of defaulting to us-east-1.

Anthropic API release notes 2026-08-27: across Python/TypeScript/Go/Java/Ruby/C# SDKs, client.beta.files and client.beta.skills stop sending the files-api-2025-04-14 and skills-2025-10-02 beta headers; 'client.beta.skills.delete() deletes a Skill together with all of its versions', and BetaSkill is renamed BetaContainerSkill.

Anthropic API release notes 2026-08-19: computer use (computer_toolset_20260801) is out of beta and 'Upgrading an existing integration changes the request shape and tool handling'; Agent Skills / Skills API and the Files API also left beta.

GitHub Changelog 2026-08-12: Agent Plugins 1.0 published 2026-08-06 as a multi-vendor open standard (AWS, Anysphere, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel, Google); 'Existing GitHub Copilot plugins that don't target Agent Plugins 1.0 remain supported, with no migration required.'

GitHub Changelog (announced 2026-07-31, effective 2026-09-01): six Copilot models retired (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Raptor Mini); 'Please update your workflows and integrations to use the supported model before these dates'; administrators must enable alternative models via policy before they appear in selectors.

Gemini API changelog in-window entries (2026-08-13 Gemini 3.7 Flash GA, 2026-08-26 Gemini 3.5 Transcribe GA, 2026-08-27 Gemini Omni Flash GA) contain no agent-breaking or permission-model change; the temperature/top_p/top_k sampling deprecation is dated 2026-07-21, outside the window.
inferences: Two independent vendors patching shell allow-rule parsing in the same 21-day window indicates a systemic class, not a one-off bug: the permission rule language is a lexical matcher over a command string, while the shell that ultimately executes has richer semantics (arithmetic assignment, dangling operators, dynamic word expansion, zsh conditionals, options matching a wildcard). Any team that hand-wrote Bash allow rules before 2026-08-20 should assume their effective permission surface is wider than intended.

Trust-gated instruction loading is a reproducibility hazard rather than only a security feature: an agent run in an untrusted checkout gets no project AGENTS.md, produces off-convention output, and gives no signal that repo rules were withheld - the operator sees 'the agent ignored our rules', not 'the harness suppressed them'.

The 2026-08-27 SDK beta-namespace unification widens the blast radius of an unchanged call site: code calling client.beta.skills.delete() deletes all versions after the SDK bump. This is the failure shape most likely to slip past an AI-driven dependency upgrade, since the call site diff is empty.

Anthropic Python SDK v1.0 removing temperature/top_p/top_k is a near-certain generator of C06 failures: every model trained before 2026-08-20 will keep emitting those kwargs for the Anthropic SDK, and the failure appears at runtime, not at lint time.

Claude Code --restricted and Codex's Guardian strict-review notification are converging vendor answers to over-broad agent authority (I03): the response is shifting from 'grant narrowly' to 'run the whole agent in a reduced-capability mode', which also neutralises the settings-file escalation path since --restricted ignores user/project/local settings.

The codex mcp-server deprecation pushes cross-agent interop from a neutral protocol endpoint toward vendor-specific plugins (the Codex plugin for Claude Code), pulling in the K08 direction, while Agent Plugins 1.0 pushes the opposite way; the net effect on fragmentation in this window is ambiguous.

Codex extensions being able to 'inspect or replace MCP tool results before they reach the model' creates a trusted-path interception point: an extension can rewrite tool output the model reasons over, without touching the MCP server or the prompt. This expands the I07 surface from 'malicious server' to 'malicious result rewriter'.

records.title: Shell許可ルールの解釈が実際のシェル意味論とずれ、書いた権限境界と実効境界が一致しない
records.summary: Agent harnesses match Bash allow/deny rules lexically against a command string, while the shell that executes it has richer semantics. In this window both vendors patched divergences: Claude Code auto-approved arithmetic assignments such as OPTIND=1/0, mis-handled dangling && / || operators, and warned that an allow rule like Bash(git * main) also matches arbitrary options; Codex began requiring approval for commands containing dynamic shell words. The failure is silent - the operator believes a narrow rule is in force while a crafted or merely malformed command slips past the classifier. Unlike a harness vulnerability, the remediation lands on the user: every hand-written Bash allow rule predating 2026-08-20 must be re-audited, not just upgraded past.

evidence.summary: v2.1.251 'Fixed Bash permission checks auto-approving commands that assign an arithmetic expression to an integer shell variable (e.g. OPTIND=1/0)'; v2.1.246 'always require approval for malformed commands with a dangling && or || operator' plus a startup warning that wildcard-before-subcommand allow rules 'also match options'; v2.1.238 improved checking for zsh-specific conditional syntax.

evidence.title: ChatGPT & Codex changelog, 2026-08-20
evidence.summary: 'Require approval for commands with dynamic shell words' - independent vendor patching the same class of allowlist evasion in the same window.

records.notes: Checked I03 (permissions granted too broadly), I12 (approval fatigue), I16 (harness vulnerability), I17 (agent bypasses normal process). I03 assumes the grant itself is wide; here the grant is correctly narrow and the matcher is wrong. I16 is the closest but its practical response is 'upgrade the agent', whereas this requires auditing user-authored allow rules whose meaning was never what the author intended. Two independent vendors in one 21-day window supports treating it as a class.

records.title: Workspace trust状態がAGENTS.md/MCP設定の読み込みを無言で左右し、同じRepositoryでもAgentの挙動が変わる
records.summary: Harnesses now gate which project-level instruction and configuration files load on a workspace trust flag. Codex stopped supplying project-level AGENTS.md instructions in untrusted projects on 2026-08-20; Claude Code v2.1.238 made a headersHelper declared in a project .mcp.json, plugin, or agent file require folder trust. The agent gives no visible signal that repo rules were withheld, so the same repository and the same prompt produce convention-violating output in a fresh or untrusted checkout - CI runners, ephemeral cloud sessions, and newly cloned worktrees being the common triggers. Operators diagnose it as 'the agent ignored our CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md' and start rewriting instructions that were never read.

records.title: 権限チェック後にpathが差し替わる／checkより先に読むことで、deny規則が実効しない
records.summary: Claude Code v2.1.251 fixed a cluster of bypasses in which the permission decision and the filesystem access referred to different objects: Read/Write/Edit followed a symlink swapped inside the working directory after the permission check; Grep and Glob did not apply Read(...) deny rules through symlinked search paths; the Workflow tool read (and quoted in error text) a scriptPath outside the readable set before the permission check ran; and plugin commands could point outside the plugin directory via path traversal. Configured deny rules such as **/.env were therefore advisory rather than enforced for some tool paths.

evidence.title: claude-code CHANGELOG v2.1.251
evidence.summary: 'Fixed file tools (Read, Write, Edit) following a symlink swapped inside the working directory after the permission check'; Grep/Glob not applying Read(...) deny rules through symlinked search paths; 'Fixed the Workflow tool reading (and quoting in errors) a scriptPath outside what the session may read before the permission check ran'; plugin commands pointing outside the plugin directory via path traversal.

records.notes: Same mechanism, artifact and practical response as I16 (intrusion via a vulnerability in the sandbox / extension / agent itself): the fix is to upgrade to v2.1.251+. Filed as an update rather than a new problem, but worth recording on I16 that deny rules were demonstrably non-enforcing for symlinked and pre-check read paths before 2026-08-28, so any team that relied on **/.env-style deny rules for secret protection should treat pre-2.1.251 sessions as having had unverified access.

records.title: Provider fix: Agent全体を低権限モードで起動する選択肢（--restricted）が追加された
records.summary: Claude Code v2.1.248 added --restricted / CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED=1, which removes the built-in tools that run commands or code plus WebFetch, restricts file access to the working directory, refuses bypassPermissions, and ignores user, project and local settings. Codex added client notification when Guardian requires strict review. This shifts the answer to over-broad agent authority from per-rule narrowing toward a whole-session capability floor, and notably closes the settings-file escalation path because --restricted ignores settings entirely - which also makes it a workaround-obsoleting change for teams that previously wrapped agents in external sandboxes just to strip execution tools.

records.title: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODELの意味がoverrideからdefaultへ変更され、既存設定のsubagent modelが黙って変わる
records.summary: Claude Code v2.1.251 changed CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL to set the default subagent model rather than override everything, so an agent definition's model: field and an explicit per-spawn model now take precedence. Teams that set the env var to force every subagent onto a cheap model - a common cost-control workaround - silently lose that guarantee on upgrade wherever an agent file pins a model, changing both spend and output quality with no config edit and no error. The same release added PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch hooks that can block, confirm, or annotate a model switch, which is the new supported control point.
